items.title: News Analysis: Can Israeli opposition's legislative offensive break coalition deadlock?
text: JERUSALEM, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Israel's opposition launched a legislative offensive as the 26th Knesset convened earlier this week, seeking to reverse many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies, limit prime ministerial terms and establish a state commission of inquiry into the Hamas-led attack of Oct. 7, 2023.

Analysts say the move is intended to deliver on campaign promises, take the parliamentary initiative and increase pressure on Netanyahu, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot works to form a new government. However, deep divisions over security, religion and cooperation with Arab parties are likely to complicate both the legislative push and efforts to build a governing coalition.

Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and the left-wing Democrats have submitted proposals seeking to repeal legislation that weakens the attorney general's authority, reform the judicial selection committee and overhaul media regulation.

The bills are widely seen as targeting Netanyahu's judicial overhaul, launched in 2023, which sparked months of mass protests as opponents warned that the reforms would undermine judicial independence and weaken democratic checks and balances.
The opposition also seeks an independent state inquiry into the Oct. 7 attack, a demand Netanyahu's government has resisted, citing concerns over potential political bias.
Analysts say such an inquiry could examine failures across Israel's political, intelligence and military establishments, potentially intensifying scrutiny of Netanyahu's role and responsibility.
Other proposals include limiting prime ministers to eight years in office and revising rules governing a premier's incapacitation.
The Democrats also introduced bills allowing public transportation on the Jewish Sabbath, civil marriage and expanded equality protections.
While these measures appeal to secular and liberal voters, they could complicate negotiations with religious parties whose support Eisenkot may need.
The opposition's push signals a shift in the political winds following Israel's Oct. 27 election.

Netanyahu's right-wing bloc secured 53 seats in the 120-member parliament, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's four-party alliance and 19 for two Arab-led parties. Together, Netanyahu's opponents command 67 seats but remain divided over whether and how to form a government.
President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government on Nov. 8, but the former military chief has yet to put together a viable governing coalition.

Unlike the formation of a government, individual bills can advance through shifting parliamentary alliances, allowing opposition parties to join forces on specific issues without having to agree on a shared governing platform.
The Washington Post pointed out that the opposition's proposals seek to dismantle key elements of Netanyahu's political legacy and increase scrutiny of his administration.

On Wednesday, lawmakers voted 63-50 to establish a parliamentary arrangements committee chaired by a Yashar lawmaker, an early indication that Netanyahu's opponents can translate their numerical advantage into institutional influence.

items.title: Putin proposes humanitarian mission in eastern Ukraine during talks with U.S. envoys
text: MOSCOW, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday proposed organizing a humanitarian mission to evacuate civilians from Kostiantynivka in eastern Ukraine, drawing on previous experience in Oleshky.

Speaking during talks in Moscow with U.S. presidential special envoy Steve Witkoff and U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, Putin said hundreds of civilians remained in the city and called for their evacuation.
Located in the Donetsk region, Kostiantynivka had served as a key Ukrainian military stronghold. Russia claimed to have taken full control of the city in July.

On territorial issues, Putin said Russia would recognize "only the state border" as the line of demarcation with Ukraine. He reiterated Moscow's opposition to the deployment of foreign troops in Ukraine, warning that such forces would pose a threat to Russia's national security and become legitimate military targets.

Putin also said Moscow has never opposed dialogue with Europe, but European countries has severed contacts with Russia. He expressed hope that Washington would work with European countries to promote peace, and stressed the need for a lasting settlement of the Ukraine conflict.

Russian forces continued strikes on Ukrainian military-industrial and energy facilities using ground-based precision-guided weapons and long-range attack drones, the Russian Defense Ministry said Thursday.

Russian forces struck drone production and assembly plants in Kiev and the surrounding region, as well as facilities in the Kiev region producing solid rocket fuel components for operational-tactical missiles and solid-fuel boosters for drones, it said.

On the same day, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine would never recognize Russia's occupation of its territories, regardless of any decision made by the United States, the Interfax-Ukraine news agency reported.

"We must make it clear that we will never, under any circumstances, recognize Russia's occupation of Ukrainian territory," Zelensky told the plenary session of the European Political Community summit.
On Wednesday, Zelensky said Ukraine could not agree to withdraw from the Donbas region to end the conflict, because the issue concerns the country's independence.  ■

items.title: Chinese fishing vessel rescues 3 PNG citizens
text: This photo taken with a mobile phone shows an ambulance being called to send the rescued Papua New Guineans to a hospital for health checks at the Majuro port, the Marshall Islands, on Nov. 12, 2026. A Chinese fishing vessel has successfully rescued three Papua New Guineans on the high seas near the Marshall Islands, the Chinese Embassy in Papua New Guinea told Xinhua on Friday. (Hua Nan Yu 702/Handout via Xinhua)

MELBOURNE, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese fishing vessel has successfully rescued three Papua New Guineans on the high seas near the Marshall Islands, the Chinese Embassy in Papua New Guinea told Xinhua on Friday.
Chinese fishing vessel Hua Nan Yu 702 found a disabled PNG boat on Tuesday in waters near the Marshall Islands, an embassy spokesperson told Xinhua.

The boat carried three PNG citizens from Namatanai, New Ireland Province, Papua New Guinea, who had been drifting at sea since Oct. 29. The Chinese fishing vessel rescued them and provided them with necessary food and shelter.
After rescuing the three PNG citizens, the Chinese fishing vessel immediately suspended its scheduled operations and transported them to the nearest port in the Marshall Islands.

On Thursday, the fishing vessel arrived at the port of Majuro in the Marshall Islands and handed over the rescued Papua New Guineans and their boat to officials from the PNG government in the presence of Marshall Islands officials.
The PNG officials expressed gratitude to the Chinese vessel for rescuing the three people.
The three were then taken to a hospital for health checks.

items.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after thousands of flights disrupted
text: WASHINGTON, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday evening after hours of disruption affected thousands of flights across the country.
Flight cancellations and delays are expected to continue through the weekend.

At a press conference, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the country's "incredibly old" air traffic control system for the nationwide ground stop. He asked Congress for 50 billion U.S. dollars in emergency funding to overhaul the aging air traffic control infrastructure.

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, who was also at the press conference Friday evening, said that while nothing was completely certain at that point, there were no indications that a cyberattack was responsible.
Earlier, Duffy said on the social media platform X that the FAA had issued the nationwide ground stop following a "communication issue" impacting all air route traffic control centers.
U.S. media reported that the FAA had issued an advisory citing "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety" as grounds for the nationwide ground stop, describing it as a rare move.
More than 10,000 flights were disrupted, according to a report by CNBC, which noted that more flight cancellations were expected to extend into Saturday.

U.S. President Donald Trump said the nationwide ground stop does not appear to be the result of a cyberattack or artificial intelligence, according to Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy.

"It doesn't seem like that," Doocy told "The Ingraham Angle" after speaking with Trump by phone. Trump believed that the disruption appeared to stem from "a bunch of old broken stuff" that the FAA relies on to keep air travel operating.

Earlier on Friday, Eurocontrol said that all flights departing from its member states for U.S. airports were suspended at the request of the FAA. The suspension covers departures between 2200 GMT on Friday and 0500 GMT on Saturday.
The U.S. nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

items.title: China expects greater consensus, more tangible outcomes with APEC parties: spokesperson
text: BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- China looks forward to building further consensus among parties of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), achieving more tangible outcomes, and injecting robust impetus into prosperity and growth in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Friday.
Spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a regular press briefing when answering a query related to the upcoming 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province.

Noting that after 12 years, China is once again hosting APEC, Mao said the APEC "China Year" has yielded fruitful outcomes. China has successfully held over 300 meetings and events by focusing on the theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together" and the three priority areas of "Openness, Innovation, and Cooperation."

More than 10,000 representatives have participated in the events and reached a number of common understandings on cooperation, laying a solid foundation for the upcoming meeting, said the spokesperson.

With this APEC meeting set to open next week, Mao said China looks forward to agreeing on the APEC Shenzhen Leaders' Declaration among all member economies as well as more practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: China's top diplomat meets U.S. representatives attending political dialogue
text: Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, meets with U.S. representatives attending the U.S.-China Political Dialogue 2026 in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Tian Yu)
BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- China's top diplomat Wang Yi on Friday met with U.S. representatives attending the U.S.-China Political Dialogue 2026 in Beijing.

Wang, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, said that China and the United States should clarify the goals of their joint efforts, expand the areas of mutually beneficial cooperation, consolidate the foundation of bilateral relations, and be committed to maintaining world peace and stability.

The two sides should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and win-win cooperation, and implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state on building a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity, Wang noted.

The representative of the U.S. side said that people-to-people and cultural exchanges, especially those between young people and students, are conducive to enhancing friendship and mutual trust between the two peoples, adding that they are grateful for the invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and study in the coming five years, and are willing to make efforts to promote the healthy and stable development of U.S.-China relations.

items.title: Chinese premier calls for improving multi-tiered social security system
text: Chinese Premier Li Qiang presides over a State Council study session on improving the multi-tiered social security system and further strengthening the social security safety net on Nov. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen)

BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Thursday called for further deepening social security reform and improving a multi-tiered social security system that covers the entire population in both urban and rural areas and is fair and unified, safe and well-regulated, and sustainable.
Li made the remarks while presiding over a State Council study session on improving the multi-tiered social security system and further strengthening the social security safety net.

China has basically established the world's largest and fully functional social security system. Yet changes in the demographic structure, technological progress and diverse forms of employment have placed new and higher demands on the development of the social security system, Li said.
He noted that the country must proceed from its own realities, balance doing the best with doing what is possible, and raise social security levels steadily as the economy develops.

Li also underlined the need to clarify the responsibilities of the government, employers, individuals and society, so that responsibilities are properly shared and a long-term mechanism of mutual assistance is formed. While meeting basic needs and providing a safety net, the system should offer more varied forms of provision to meet people's multi-tiered and diverse needs.

He called for accelerating efforts to address weak links, expand coverage of enterprise annuities, make the personal pension scheme more attractive, support the growth of commercial health insurance, and steadily advance the long-term care insurance system.

He said greater attention should be given to people in flexible employment and new forms of employment, with improvements to their social security arrangements, a gradual increase in participation rates, and stronger protection of their rights and interests.

Li also highlighted the need to make the social security system fairer, steadily raise pension protection for urban and rural residents, make better use of unemployment insurance, improve the tiered and classified social assistance system, and refine the social welfare system.

He added that supervision of the social security fund should be strengthened, the fund's value preserved and increased, and relevant laws and regulations revised in a timely manner to provide stronger legal support.

items.title: China proving a place where ideas can take shape
text: This photo taken on Nov. 10, 2026 shows the south square of the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), the main venue of the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE), in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Wang Xiang)
BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- From abstract concepts to market-ready goods, many global innovations are undergoing transformation in China.

At the just-concluded ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in east China's Shanghai, HaptonTech demonstrated how a programmable touch pad helps bring closer a future in which online shoppers will be able to feel the texture of what they see through touch-responsive screens before placing an order.

Originally conceived to help visually impaired people interact with digital devices, this technology enables flat surfaces to change shape and produce tactile sensations, with potential applications in sectors ranging from digital interfaces to robotics and medical equipment.

For Mert Orhan Astam, founder of the four-person Dutch startup, making the CIIE debut was about finding partners to commercialize the technology. China, in his view, is an obvious destination. "People here are willing to try new things," he said.
The company is in talks with a Chinese robotics firm regarding a joint project and is seeking manufacturing and research partners to explore commercial uses of the material.

This example illustrates a broader story unfolding among early-stage ventures from abroad coming to China: if ideas can find the right partners and industrial ecosystems here, they have much better chances of becoming real products.

This photo taken on Nov. 10, 2026 shows the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), the main venue of the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE), in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Wang Xiang)

At the ninth CIIE, the world's largest import-themed expo, which concluded on Tuesday, many exhibitors displayed prototypes, sought feedback and tested whether China's industrial landscape could help them move faster and further.

Hanray Tech, a chip startup assisted by British-funded business incubator Entrepreneur Groundwork Guide (EGG), was one of them. Its founding team, which includes PhDs from the University of California and the University of Oxford, started with just three people.
"When the project first came to China, we helped it connect with government resources, financing channels and industrial partners," said Deng Junyin, international director of EGG China.

The company is now valued at around 1.7 billion yuan (about 253 million U.S. dollars), and its team has grown from three people to more than 80. It plans to build a mass-production base in Shanghai's Jiading District to take advantage of the local industrial ecosystem.

"What stands out first is China's openness and inclusiveness. The country welcomes technologies from around the world and helps them take root, continue R&D and scale up here," said Deng, adding that targeted policy support, efficient services and mature manufacturing bases also make a big difference.

COMAC's electric aircraft completes first piloted test flight
text: China's first domestically developed 10-metric-ton-class electric commercial aircraft, the CE-25A, completed its first piloted test flight in Binzhou, Shandong province, on Saturday, marking another milestone in the development of electric aircraft for short-haul commercial travel.

The aircraft, developed by Commercial Aircraft Corp of China, carried two pilots and a flight test engineer. The test lasted 57 minutes and 46 seconds, including 16 minutes and 38 seconds in the air, during which the aircraft covered 60.4 kilometers.
The aircraft performed normally and all test results met expectations, COMAC said in a statement.

The CE-25A is COMAC's first electric commercial aircraft, designed to carry 19 passengers on commercial flights between cities. It has a maximum takeoff weight of 10 metric tons, a cruising speed of 300 kilometers per hour, a cruising altitude of 2,400 meters, and a range of 400 kilometers.
The aircraft is powered by a distributed electric ducted-fan propulsion system mounted on its wings.

items.title: CSG brings energy transition solutions to COP31 China Pavilion
text: A thematic side event titled "Digital-Intelligent Innovation for Green Electricity: Building a New Power System and New Practices for Global Energy Transition" was held in Antalya, Turkiye, on Nov 13 local time, on the sidelines of the China Pavilion at COP31, officially known as the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

The event was guided by China's National Energy Administration, hosted by China Southern Power Grid (CSG), and co-organized by the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) and the Office for China-IRENA Cooperation (China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute).

Through the release of research findings, roundtable discussions and case studies, the side event showcased Chinese energy companies' innovative exploration and international practices in building a new power system, contributing Chinese expertise and solutions to the global low-carbon energy transition.

Liu Zhenmin, China's special envoy for climate change, Francesco La Camera, director-general of IRENA, Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana, under-secretary-general of the United Nations and executive secretary of the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP), Xiong Minfeng, deputy director-general of the Department of International Cooperation under National Energy Administration of China, attended the event and delivered opening remarks.

At the side event, CSG, aligning with the broader context of global energy transition and climate governance, presented its achievements in building a new power system through systematic innovation practices.

A highlight of the event was the joint release by CSG, IRENA and the China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute of "Solutions for building a new power system: The role of grids, storage and hydropower". The report systematically reviews the technical requirements arising from high shares of renewable energy and increasing electrification, and introduces solutions and practical experience from early-moving countries.

The Global Energy Storage Alliance Initiative was officially launched by CSG Energy Storage, the China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute and the China Energy Storage Alliance, together with leading domestic and international enterprises, with several international institutions and industry organizations expressing their intention to join.
As a representative unit of the alliance, CSG Energy Storage outlined how advances in energy storage can support the development of new power systems.

CSG released for the first time the Chinese and English editions of the CSG White Paper on Green Development, comprehensively presenting the company's achievements during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-25) in clean energy supply, green and low-carbon operations, and electricity-carbon coupling business, and outlining plans to further develop three key areas — a new power system, new energy systems, and a new-type power grid — during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-30).

items.title: FM calls for mutual respect and win-win cooperation
text: China is not the United States and will not become another US, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Friday, stressing that the two major countries are fully capable of pursuing mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and win-win cooperation.

Wang made the remarks during a meeting with US representatives attending the US-China Political Dialogue 2026, quoting an ancient Chinese saying about "all things growing together without harming one another, and different paths running in parallel without conflicting with the other".
He said that the dialogue has been held 15 times since its launch in 2010, and has played a positive role in deepening mutual understanding.

Wang urged both sides to translate the important consensus reached between the leaders of the two countries into concrete policies and actions, saying that Beijing and Washington should embrace harmony while respecting differences, view each other objectively and rationally, and develop stable, positive expectations for China-US relations in the long term.

He called for expanding dialogue and cooperation in science and technology, artificial intelligence and other fields for mutual benefit, and opposed the abuse of the concept of security and excessive politicization.
People-to-people exchanges underpin relations between countries, Wang said, urging sustained efforts to expand exchanges, particularly among young people and students.
He also called on both nations to fulfill their international obligations, and act with the responsibility expected of major countries in safeguarding world peace.

Representatives of the delegation — led by former US ambassador to China and former senator Max Baucus — said the two countries should strengthen cooperation in areas such as trade and AI, and build greater mutual trust.

They said that exchanges between the two peoples, especially young people and students, could foster friendship and trust. They expressed appreciation for President Xi Jinping's initiative to invite 100,000 US youth to visit China for exchanges and study over the next five years, saying they were willing to contribute to the healthy and stable development of US-China relations.

In an interview during the dialogue, Michael Hart, president of the Beijing-based American Chamber of Commerce in China, said that interactions between the two heads of state this year offered an important opportunity to steer bilateral ties toward a more positive direction.
"The two leaders have set the tone," Hart said, adding that he hoped to see more working-level exchanges and cooperation in 2027.
"We need more discussions between US and China leaders at every level," he said, calling for broader engagement involving political leaders, business executives, students and other organizations.

Jeffrey Lehman, vice-chancellor of New York University Shanghai and chair of the board of governors of AmCham Shanghai, said the recent stabilization of China-US relations was particularly important for the chamber's roughly 1,000 member companies, which needed a predictable environment to plan investments and organize supply chains.

items.title: Envoy: APEC meeting boosts cooperation
text: The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen is expected to create new opportunities for regional economic cooperation, with the Republic of Korea and China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region making contributions, a diplomat from the ROK said.

"I hope that the upcoming APEC (meeting) in Shenzhen will provide fresh momentum for regional cooperation, instilling greater confidence in businesses seeking to diversify their investments and build solid partnerships," said Seo Man-kyo, consul general of the ROK in Hong Kong.

With the ROK and HKSAR both APEC economies, Seo told China Daily that the two members can make meaningful contributions by supporting an open, predictable trade environment and enabling more businesses and individuals to benefit from digital transformation, backed by legal and institutional stability.

The APEC meeting will be held on Nov 18 and 19 in Shenzhen, a city in South China's Guangdong province adjoining the HKSAR, under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together". It marks the third time China is hosting the top APEC event.

Apart from practical cooperation such as providing accessible and reliable information to businesses, coordinating trade procedures, and opportunities across markets, Seo said digitalization cooperation covering e-commerce, digital trade and fintech is also important for the ROK and HKSAR.

"I would particularly like to emphasize the role of SMEs (small and medium-sized enterprises) and the youth demographic," said Seo, noting the need to empower them to participate more fully in the opportunities provided by regional integration.

Before assuming his role as the ROK's envoy to the HKSAR in early October, Seo had visited the city more than 60 times as a seasoned China expert who spent over 30 years in Beijing's economic and business sector, and served as the vice-chairman of the Korean Chamber of Commerce in China and a research fellow at the Center for Korean Peninsula Studies at the Peking University.
Through the visits, Seo said he had come to appreciate Hong Kong's economic vitality as an international metropolis, as well as the professional expertise and capabilities of its people.
"Hong Kong serves as a crucial nexus connecting (South) Korea, the Chinese mainland, and the wider world," said Seo.
The ROK and HKSAR were each other's 7th largest trading partner in 2025, according to Hong Kong's Trade and Industry Department.

Hong Kong is also an important entrepot for merchandise trade between ROK and the Chinese mainland. Re-export trade between the two economies through the SAR amounted to HK$381.7 billion ($48.65 billion) in 2025.
Noting Hong Kong's position as a "superconnector", Seo said he looks beyond logistics and goods to professional services that businesses need when entering new markets.

The ROK's technological prowess, innovative production and ideas can synergize with Hong Kong's capital, professional services, and global networks to unlock potential in the Chinese mainland and beyond, Seo said, adding that he also seeks two-way connections helping Hong Kong enterprises find partners in the ROK.

items.title: Museum expo aims to strengthen intl exchanges
text: The 11th Chinese Exposition of Museums and Relevant Products and Technologies opened on Friday in the coastal city of Haikou, capital of Hainan province, with Egypt serving as the expo's first-ever country of honor — a move that experts said signals a broader push to strengthen international museum exchanges.

As the largest and most influential expo in China's museum sector, the event has been held biennially since 2004. This year, it brings together almost 600 museums and around 200 cultural heritage-related enterprises in Haikou, showcasing cutting-edge advances in the protection of cultural relics, digital museums, exhibition display technology and cultural creative products.
The theme this year is "Museums for High-Quality Development: Empowering with Technology, Connecting with the Future".

The four-day event features 12 thematic areas, including achievements in museum development, digital and intelligent technologies, international exhibitors, non-State-owned museums and cultural heritage corporations.

The expo introduced a country-of-honor mechanism, with Egypt serving in this capacity. Three major Egyptian cultural institutions — the Grand Egyptian Museum, the Egyptian Museum in Cairo and the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization — are taking part in the international exhibitors' area. French institutions, including Universcience — Cite des Sciences et de l'Industrie in Paris, are also exhibiting.

Guan Qiang, president of the Chinese Museums Association, said that while the expo had previously hosted foreign museums, no participating nation had been given the status of a country of honor. By introducing this format, the organizers hope to strengthen future exchanges with the museum sectors of other countries.

items.title: Hong Kong's offshore RMB bond market gathers pace
text: Hong Kong's offshore renminbi bond market is poised for further expansion after the Chinese yuan became the leading currency for bond issuances in the city's listed bond market, industry executives and academics said, citing lower borrowing costs and a resilient currency attracting global issuers and investors.

Data released earlier this month by rating agency Dagong Global Hong Kong showed that offshore RMB bonds — also known as dim sum bonds — accounted for 37 percent of listed bond issuances by value in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in the first nine months of 2026, overtaking the United States dollar's 33 percent share. At 117 issuances, RMB-denominated bonds also led by number.

Building on that momentum, Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Ltd is scheduled to launch its HKEX Offshore RMB Bond Index on Monday, which will serve as a reference for market trends and as an underlying index for exchange-traded funds.

Lower borrowing costs remain a major draw. "The renminbi, particularly in the offshore market, has become one of the world's cheapest funding currencies. This cost advantage is what matters," Gan Tian, CEO of China Asset Management (Hong Kong) Ltd, said in an interview with China Daily.

Global technology giants have been tapping bond markets worldwide as spending on artificial intelligence drives their financing needs, he said, adding that some have paid more than 7 percent to borrow for 30 years in the US market.
Gan said he expects some of these companies to sell dim sum bonds in Hong Kong within the next 12 months, and that investment banks in the city are already approaching prospective borrowers.

The First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the HKSAR (2026-2030), released in September, calls for strengthening the city's role as the world's largest offshore RMB hub by expanding the dim sum bond market and broadening the range of maturities.
With policy support adding momentum, Gan said the dim sum bond boom is "only just beginning", and predicted "explosive growth" over the next few years.

He said he expects Hong Kong's offshore RMB liquidity pool to grow from about 1 trillion yuan ($150 billion) to at least 5 trillion yuan by the end of 2030, and the dim sum bond market to expand from 2.6 trillion yuan to at least 10 trillion yuan.

Rocky Tung Yat-ngok, executive director of Hong Kong's Financial Services Development Council, said that many foreign issuers are considering Hong Kong, "and these issuers aren't only sovereign issuers, but also multilateral development banks and companies from developed markets".
Some of these development banks have never explored issuing bonds in Hong Kong, or borrowing in RMB, Tung said, underscoring the potential to attract new issuers.
Investor demand is also strengthening. The yuan has gained more than 4 percent against the US dollar this year, even as currencies including the euro and yen have weakened.
Gan, from China Asset Management, said that expectations of stability and appreciation are encouraging more overseas institutional investors to allocate funds to dim sum bonds.

items.title: China’s Short Dramas See Quality Shift With AI-Made Historical Hit
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019262/China’s Short Dramas See Quality Shift With AI-Made Historical Hit
text: An AI-generated short drama made by amateurs, including a former rideshare driver and a stay-at-home mother, has gone viral in China for its high production quality and historical accuracy, challenging the genre’s reputation for simple, brainless plots.

First released in August, “Armed Into the Song Dynasty” already has 10 seasons and comprises roughly 1,000 3-minute episodes. As of Thursday, the show has amassed over 12 billion views across platforms including Douyin, China’s version of TikTok, and streaming site Bilibili, local media reported.

In the first nine months of this year, 490,000 micro-dramas were released in China, 13 times more than in all of 2025. AI is also reshaping the micro-drama industry, with AI-generated productions now accounting for more than 90% of all such content, according to a report the National Radio and Television Administration released in October. The report also found that China’s short-drama audience had surpassed 600 million active monthly viewers.

Adapted from a web novel published in installments beginning this April by a writer under the pen name Chagen’er, “Armed Into the Song Dynasty” follows five modern-day soldiers who unwittingly travel back to the late Northern Song dynasty (960–1127), bringing their weapons and military expertise with them.

The late Northern Song period is a popular setting for Chinese time-travel fiction, as it offers viewers an alternative reality to the dynasty’s end, when invading Jurchen tribes captured two of its emperors — widely remembered as a national disgrace.

Fans have praised the drama’s carefully crafted script, elaborate fight scenes, and rounded characters who grapple with everything from the imperial examination system to weapons, food, and military equipment shortages during invasions by northern nomadic groups.
The historical details have prompted some viewers to look up Song-era official ranks, military organizations, and historical records and compare them against the drama’s depictions.

The production team behind “Armed Into the Song Dynasty” reportedly comprises six members — including a former pharmaceutical sales representative, interior designer, rideshare driver, stay-at-home mother, and wholesale business owner — who met during an online course on how to use AI to make short dramas.

Zhang Hansheng, 54, the production team’s head, told domestic media that the series has so far cost roughly 1 million yuan ($150,000) to produce, but declined to disclose the team’s earnings. However, rumors of hefty returns have drawn fresh attention to AI drama production, which many see as a potential source of new opportunities for grassroots content creators.

In the comments on a video interview with Zhang by the domestic outlet Yicai, some viewers said the project had inspired them to learn AI tools and try making dramas themselves. Others urged caution, noting the rise of scams disguised as AI-related courses.

The show’s success comes as the genre shifts toward higher production values. Until recently, short dramas were widely considered mindless entertainment defined by exaggerated interpersonal conflicts, formulaic characters, and implausible plots.

items.title: How ‘Anxious China’ Changed Its Mind About Psychotherapy
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019263/How ‘Anxious China’ Changed Its Mind About Psychotherapy
text: Editor’s note: Zhang Li is a professor of anthropology at the University of California, Davis, and the author of “Anxious China: Inner Revolution and Politics of Psychotherapy,” which explores how a new psychotherapeutic culture is taking root in China amid profound socioeconomic change. A Chinese version of the book was released this summer. Here, Zhang, who grew up in Kunming, capital of the southwestern Yunnan province, talks with The Paper about her personal journey, trends in mental health care, and the potential impact of artificial intelligence.

The Paper: In your book, you say that returning home to Kunming to conduct research into the city’s mental and psychological landscape was a “deeply emotional experience” that sometimes left you feeling vulnerable. How did your personal connection with Kunming shape this project?

Zhang: The idea for the book first came to me when I learned that my best friend from middle school had become a therapist. I was quite surprised. This was around 2000, when interest in psychology was just beginning to take off in China and few people knew anything about mental health counseling. When I talked to my friend about her work, I realized that it touched on all kinds of everyday issues but was relatively unexplored. Most of the anthropological field research I’d come across had been conducted outside China.

As I worked on the project, I discovered how deeply it was connected to my family. My mother died 13 years ago. Looking back, I realized she’d lived with post-traumatic stress disorder for much of her life. She lost her mother when she was 8 years old. Her father remarried, and her stepmother treated her and her siblings very badly.

Growing up, we became accustomed to her extreme emotional reactions, but we had no idea they were symptomatic of a psychological disorder. Back then, people simply described this behavior as having “a bad temper.” It was only after reading up on the subject that I came to understand that my mother had suffered from chronic anxiety and depression, but she lacked the language to express it.

Seeing a psychiatrist is more normalized now; back then, mental health was a taboo topic. When I began my fieldwork, my mother was 80. I repeatedly urged her to see a psychiatrist, and eventually she agreed. After a complicated and rather haphazard diagnostic process, she was prescribed a short course of Prozac, which helped improve her condition. In the final three years of her life, she was relatively at peace, and we could have calmer, more constructive conversations.

I chose Kunming for my fieldwork because it allowed me to leverage personal connections and familiarity with the local environment. In addition, scholars were already conducting similar research in major cities such as Beijing and Shanghai, so I wanted to look at a medium-sized city. Kunming was experiencing many of the same problems as larger cities amid China’s economic reforms and social transformation. Rapid, large-scale change inevitably causes disruption, and the psychological disruption individuals experience manifests in all kinds of ways.

items.title: China’s Hospital Companions Learn Where to Draw the Line
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019255/China’s Hospital Companions Learn Where to Draw the Line
text: SHANGHAI — When prospective clients contacted Li Shuping’s medical companion agency in Shanghai, their first question often had little to do with the hospital visit they were arranging.

“Patients used to ask first whether we were individuals or a legitimate agency,” Li tells Sixth Tone. Patients hire her company, Qingbeihu, to send a trained companion with them to hospital, helping with appointments, consultations, and paperwork.

The agency opened in September 2025, when almost anyone could advertise the same service on social media. And with people aged 60 or older accounting for 23% of China’s population by the end of 2025 and 59 million forecast to need care by 2030, more families were turning to companions to guide elderly relatives through hospital visits.

But written contracts were often absent, leaving services and fees unclear. Some patients faced unexpected charges once a visit was underway, with little recourse if they disputed them, prompting calls for tighter oversight.

But since Shanghai announced new rules for medical companion services effective July 1, Qingbeihu has received more inquiries, Li says. “Orders are growing steadily, and prospective clients seem more willing to trust the service.”

The rules cover medical companion services for Shanghai residents aged 60 and older and set requirements for worker qualifications, pricing transparency, and written contracts. They also require companions to wear identity badges, provide public lists of qualified agencies, and define responsibilities that include helping patients communicate with doctors and offering psychological support.

More recently, a national standard that took effect Nov. 1 covers medical companion services for patients of all ages across China. It also sets limits on what companions can do, prohibiting them from giving medical advice or making treatment decisions on patients’ behalf.

Following Shanghai’s new rules, Li says Qingbeihu now uses written risk and privacy agreements with patients and companions, as well as accident insurance for companions. For elderly clients unfamiliar with digital services, the agency also provides paper consent forms before a visit.
“Elderly people are very willing to have young people accompany them to seek care — it is also a kind of emotional support,” Li says.
For Qingbeihu’s six full-time companions, all under 30, the working day often begins as early as 5 a.m.

By the time Li Suyu, not related to Li Shuping, meets a patient at the hospital around 7:30 a.m., she has already asked about their medical history, drug allergies, and mobility. She then checks registration details and organizes medical records and examination reports before the hospital opens at 8.

Once consultations begin, the 22-year-old accompanies patients to see their doctors, records treatment plans and prescribed medications, and arranges any examinations ordered. She also keeps family members informed and, after the visit, helps patients keep track of follow-up appointments and medication reminders.

items.title: Zero-Sum: Nanjing Noodle Shops Set a Price Rivals Can’t Match
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019254/Zero-Sum: Nanjing Noodle Shops Set a Price Rivals Can’t Match
text: A pair of Chinese noodle shops serving free meals sparked debate this week after their popularity reportedly disrupted neighboring shops’ business.

“Zero-Yuan Noodle Shop,” which opened two outlets last month in the densely populated Jiangning and Yuhuatai districts of Nanjing, capital of the eastern Jiangsu province, offers only one dish: noodles with braised vegetarian chicken and shiitake mushrooms. Each restaurant has around 50 seats, and since opening have been frequented mainly by middle-aged and elderly customers, according to domestic media.

Jiangning is home to a large migrant worker population, while Yuhuatai has the city’s largest public housing project. Signs outside the restaurants read, “A bowl of pure intention, with no fixed price; three meals a day, offered with warmth to those in need.”

The owner, surnamed Zhang, told domestic media he opened the shops for two reasons: promoting vegetarianism and charity. He said he had previously donated to charities and operated low-cost vegetarian restaurants but found that offering free noodles was the most effective way to achieve his philanthropic goals.

The two shops have served more than 1,000 bowls of noodles each day, Zhang said. He added that he had initially planned to open 10 stores, each serving 500 bowls a day, but demand had exceeded his expectations.
“Our idea was simple: get more people to come eat,” he said.
The topic has garnered more than 10 million views on microblogging platform Weibo, with many questioning whether the measures can genuinely help those in need.

Asked what they thought about the initiative, a local resident told domestic media, “It’s both good and bad. The good thing is that people who are genuinely struggling can come here to get a meal and meet their basic needs. The bad thing is, how can you tell who has money and who doesn’t?”
Other users suggested requiring customers to show their ID cards to exclude locals and help migrant workers.
In an interview with domestic media, Zhang rejected the idea of screening customers. “We want to give people facing difficulties a sense of dignity and respect,” he said.

Domestic media reported that one nearby restaurant’s daily revenue had fallen from 3,000 yuan ($450) to just a few hundred yuan. Another shop owner said he was considering not renewing his lease over concerns about declining customer traffic.

However, some shop owners said customer traffic along the street had already fallen after the relocation of several nearby factories. Others said the free noodle shops had not significantly affected their business.
Zhang told domestic media that affected business owners could work at his stores if they were willing.
He added that the two shops could lose up to 10 million yuan a year. The stores do not have payment QR codes, and he has also turned down donation offers from friends.

The shops have reportedly recently installed barriers to keep lines orderly and stopped providing noodle refills and napkins to discourage those who don’t truly need help from taking advantage of the offer.

items.title: What a Lost City Can Tell Us About Chinese Civilization’s ‘First Draft’
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019244/What a Lost City Can Tell Us About Chinese Civilization’s ‘First Draft’
text: Fufeng County, some 110 kilometers west of the northwestern Chinese city of Xi’an, is best known for its stunning Tang dynasty (618–907) relics, unearthed from an underground crypt beneath Famen Temple in the late 1980s.

But ask a Chinese archaeologist about Fufeng, and they’ll likely point you in another direction: toward a quiet cluster of more than 20 villages located along the border with neighboring Qishan County. There, hidden beneath unassuming farms and village houses, lies what a growing number of experts believe was the first capital of the Western Zhou (1046–771 BC) — one of China’s earliest and most important dynasties.

Known as Zhouyuan — literally “The Plains of Zhou” — its excavation sites have produced some of China’s most famous bronze ritual vessels. In the 1940s, those discoveries led archaeologist Shi Zhangru to survey the area and eventually propose that this was Qiyi, the center of Zhou culture before the Zhou toppled the Shang dynasty (c. 1600–1046 BC).

In the decades that followed, archaeologists worked on the site sporadically, uncovering large rammed-earth building foundations, cemeteries, craft workshops, bronze hoards, and oracle bones, all dating to the Zhou period.

Yet planned, continuous excavation at Zhouyuan began only at the turn of the 21st century, when the Institute of Archaeology at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS), the Shaanxi Academy of Archaeology, and Peking University’s School of Archaeology and Museology formed a joint team to systematically explore the site.

Why the delay? Part of the problem was historiographical. Chinese scholars have long relied on written texts to locate historic sites, and for more than 2,000 years historians placed the Western Zhou capital dozens of kilometers away, in a place called Fenghao, near Xi’an.

This drew attention and resources from other sites in the region, including Zhouyuan. But over the past decade or so, the joint archaeological team at Zhouyuan has made a string of breakthroughs that suggest Shi Zhangru’s near-century-old hunch might be right — and possibly even show that Zhouyuan, not Fenghao, was the Western Zhou’s first capital.

“Modern excavations are revealing more and more contradictions between the archaeological record and traditional accounts,” Cao Dazhi, a Peking University-based archaeologist and co-leader of the Zhouyuan team, wrote in a 2023 paper. Cao’s analysis attracted widespread attention in China for arguing that Zhouyuan was the Zhou capital, while the Fenghao region was merely an important hub and site of the royal hunting grounds.
But the dispute over ancient capitals may not be the biggest revelation to emerge from the Zhouyuan excavations.

While the exact significance of the discoveries remains a matter of debate even within the team, mounting evidence suggests the Zhou capital’s population was far more diverse than previously thought. In addition to the core Zhou population, it was home to large numbers of conquered Shang, as well as migrants from the northwest and south.

items.title: ‘Sisters, Stand Up!’ A Bar’s Urinals for Women Make a Splash in China
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019249/‘Sisters, Stand Up!’ A Bar’s Urinals for Women Make a Splash in China
text: “Sisters, stand up!” reads a slogan written in pink on the mirror above three pink-and-white urinals. Alongside each sits a stack of disposable paper funnels, waiting for those willing to heed the call.

The scene, reportedly captured in the women’s restroom of a bar in China’s eastern city of Wuxi, began circulating online last week, sparking debate and prompting a related hashtag to garner over 54 million views on microblogging platform Weibo as of Tuesday.

“I stood there in disbelief for two minutes, thinking I’d walked into the wrong restroom,” one user wrote on lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote, attaching photos of the urinals. “I kept checking until a cleaner confirmed it was indeed the women’s restroom.”

The user, a Wuxi resident in her 30s surnamed Shi, told domestic media she was unsure how to use the urinals as there were no instructions nearby. She said she eventually opted for a traditional squat toilet in the same restroom instead because she worried about making a mess or soiling her clothes.
“I’d actually love to try this,” one commenter wrote. “In winter, it’s a hassle to squat with all those thick, long layers on, especially when you’re also carrying a bag.”
“Better yet, let the brothers sit down,” read another comment, which received nearly 1,400 likes.

On Tuesday, a woman surnamed Tang, who runs Gungun Folk Theater, the bar where the urinals were reportedly installed, told domestic media that they were intended for women who find it difficult to squat, including those wearing long dresses or with limited mobility. “We just wanted to make things easier and give women another option,” she said.

Studies suggest that standing to urinate may be easier for pregnant women and those with knee osteoarthritis, while standing, crouching, and sitting have been found to make no significant difference to bladder emptying in healthy women.
Standing urinals are increasingly common worldwide at music festivals to save space and reduce restroom queues, and at outdoor activities where toilets are scarce.

In China, efforts to introduce standing urinals for women reportedly date back to 2004. At that time, Ye Ganlin, a retired senior engineer, spent 10,000 yuan ($1,400) developing a portable standing urinal for all genders, and offered free disposable funnels to female users. She said the idea grew out of her own experience with a spinal condition that made squatting increasingly difficult as she aged.

Her toilet was tested in busy public areas of neighboring cities Xi’an and Xianyang, in the northwestern Shaanxi province, and reportedly drew around 200 users a day. However, women were in the minority, Ye said.

In 2010, Shaanxi Normal University, also in Xi’an, installed six standing urinals for women, an initiative championed by professor Qu Yajun to conserve water. Female students welcomed the idea but said it would take practice to get used to the fixtures.

items.title: From 6G to Aerospace, New Tech Takes the Stage at CIIE
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019240/From 6G to Aerospace, New Tech Takes the Stage at CIIE
text: The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) closed in Shanghai on Tuesday after showcasing cutting-edge technologies in artificial intelligence, commercial aerospace, and innovative drugs.

The six-day event drew exhibitors from a record 162 countries, regions, and international organizations. A total of 4,142 overseas companies took part — also a record high — with more than 480 representative products making their global, Asian, or China debut.

U.S. wireless chipmaker Qualcomm exhibited the world’s first 6G terminal prototype — the first time the device has been shown publicly outside the lab. The prototype has been used in joint tests with China Mobile, China’s largest telecom operator, and Chinese telecom equipment manufacturer ZTE. The prototype will provide the foundation for 6G chips and support the technology’s commercial rollout.

The event featured an expanded medical devices and health care exhibition area, acting as the stage for the China debut of pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca’s new hypertension medication baxdrostat. The oral medication works by inhibiting the enzyme aldosterone synthase, which helps synthesize the blood pressure-regulating hormone aldosterone, and was approved in the U.S. in May.

German optical giant Zeiss also made its global debut of its new non-spherical lens PT Lunana, designed for myopia correction. Novartis, a Swiss multinational pharmaceutical company, showcased ianalumab, a drug used for treating the autoimmune illness Sjögren’s disease — also a China debut.

American electric vehicle company Tesla presented its Cybercab autonomous vehicle. Lacking a steering wheel or pedals, the vehicle relies on cameras and AI to drive. Hexagon — a global digital reality and metrology tech company — also displayed its industrial humanoid robot AEON.

Aerospace technology was also present, including the Zhuque-3 rocket developed by Chinese commercial aerospace company LandSpace. The rocket’s reusable booster, which uses liquid oxygen and methane as fuel, can land vertically, first achieved by the company in August.

Beyond showcasing new tech, the expo held its first exhibition area for 100 long-established, reputable international brands — from Canadian shoe companies to Spanish wineries — as well as hosted a trade and investment “matchmaking” conference, where companies and buyers met to sign cooperation agreements. The latter conference attracted more than 600 exhibitors and over 2,000 buyers from 59 countries and regions.
The deals reached at this year’s expo are projected to be worth a total of $85.45 billion over the coming year, up 2.3% from last year and a record high.

Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
text: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are planning to meet on the sidelines of a summit in China next week, the White House has said.

The historic meeting between the respective leaders of the US, Russia and China will take place as Trump attends the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summit in the southern city of Shenzhen, spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.
"The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous," she said.
It is understood Iran may also be discussed during the meeting of the world's biggest nuclear powers, but not Ukraine. Moscow and Beijing have yet to comment.
No agreement was expected to follow the talks, an unnamed, senior US official said, according to news agencies AP and Reuters.

Trump will arrive in Shenzhen late on Wednesday for the two-day summit between the 21 member states. He will also take part in bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday - their fourth meeting since the US president returned to office in 2025.

"President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People's Republic of China, and the president of the Russian Federation," Wales said.

She said Trump's trip, which will also include attending an Association of South-east Asian Nations (Asean) summit in the Philippines on Tuesday, would "secure historic wins to the American people and advance America's interests in the Indo Pacific".

A nuclear weapons control treaty between the US and Russia expired in February, leaving the world's biggest nuclear arsenals without major guardrails and effectively marking an end to the arms control co-operation that helped resolve the Cold War.
The UN has urged both sides to agree a new framework without delay. Trump however said he could replace the deal with a better agreement that included China, which has been building up its arsenal.
Former senior US officials and analysts told the BBC at the time that seeking Beijing and Moscow's co-operation could create major hurdles and take years.
Xi separately hosted both Putin and Trump in Beijing just days apart earlier this year, while the US president welcomed his Chinese counterpart to Washington in September.
Beijing has become a crucial trading partner for Moscow since it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which has isolated Russia and left it subject to Western sanctions.

But a controversial US deal to import Russian diesel and the suspension of sanctions targeting the biggest buyers of Moscow's oil and gas - including China - heightened European concern about the Trump administration's softening towards the Kremlin last month.

Trump and Xi have meanwhile sought to project warmer ties at summits in Beijing and Washington this year - though little significant progress appeared to have been made on key issues such as trade, their race for AI dominance, and Taiwan.
The war in Iran has also been a sticking point, with Beijing the largest buyer of Tehran's oil and its largest trade partner.

Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China
text: Leaders of the United States, China and Russia are set to hold an unprecedented three-way meeting next week, the White House has said.

US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China’s tech hub, the White House assistant press secretary confirmed in an announcement.

The talks will be held nine months after the last nuclear arms treaty between Washington and Moscow expired, leaving the world’s two countries with the largest atomic arsenals without caps for the first time in more than 50 years.
Trump has said the meeting is a chance for all three countries to reach a deal on nuclear stockpiles.

The New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START) lapsed in February. Trump then rejected Russia’s proposal to extend it for another year and demanded a “new, improved and modernised” deal that includes China.
Expectations are low. “We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement,” a senior Trump administration official told the Reuters news agency, describing the meeting as the start of a conversation.
Russia holds the most nuclear warheads, followed by the US, then China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.

Trump plans on discussing the Iran war with Xi and Putin, but will steer away from discussing Russia’s war in Ukraine, according to a senior US official who briefed reporters on condition of anonymity.
Elon Musk will also travel with Trump to China but will not attend the meeting, the official added. Trump is also not expected to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during the Asia trip.
The planned summit has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the US, Britain and the Soviet Union shaped the post-war order.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, however, dismissed the parallel, saying any agreements reached in Shenzhen cannot be imposed on others, but he still called the meeting “extremely significant”.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has voiced concern that the meeting could become a platform to discuss a Ukraine deal behind Kyiv’s back.
Trump has pursued closer ties with both leaders despite a short-lived trade war with China last year and Russia’s continuing war in Ukraine, where Washington is seeking to mediate a solution.
